summary: It is common to train Large Language Models (LLMs) for agentic tasks with Reinforcement Learning (RL) from scalar rewards. However, this throws away the fine-grained information about the environment that the agent experienced during the trial (e.g., error logs).
takeaways: Across agentic benchmarks, achieves higher held-out performance than baseline methods.
As a concrete testbed, we fix the Agentic Context Engineering () harness and train one model to act, reflect, and curate task-local playbooks.
The results suggest that agent training should optimize not only the actions in the current rollout, but also the model-written experience that future rollouts inherit.
